newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi closes first round of welfare talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi closes first round of welfare talks.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday began meeting with unions and employers to close the first round of welfare reform talks before a summer break.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu also attended the meeting with representatives of 31 groups, including employers' body Confindustria and Italy's three main unions.
Participants are expected to discuss the progress made since negotiations began in mid-June and to set a date to resume the meetings in late August or early September.

The talks are aimed at securing agreement on reducing social spending to help Italy qualify for the first round of Europe's single currency, but they have run into trouble over cuts to state pensions which unions staunchly oppose.

The government aims to reach agreement on the reforms to coincide with the presentation to parliament of the 1998 budget. The budget must be presented to legislators by September 30. -- Rome newsroom +39 6 678 2501
